slides.teacher_cue: New sound — and our first digraph. Two letters, one sound. s and h alone make /s/ and /h/. Together they make a completely new sound: /ʃ/. Lips slightly rounded, tongue body raised toward the hard palate, steady airflow — shhhh. Quieter and softer than /s/.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /ʃ/ cleanly and understand that sh is a digraph — two letters, one sound.
slides.correction_move: Model /s/ then /ʃ/ — contrast the tongue position and width of airstream. Students copy. Then introduce the digraph concept: these two letters are a team.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /s/ substitution and for students trying to say both /s/ and /h/ separately.

slides.observation_note: Listen for whether students can carry the focus from isolation into a real word.
